title: fix(traffic): correct shared accounting and deployed port synchronization
recorded_scope:
## Summary

Fix shared-instance received/sent undercount and the requested changed-port sync defect in this same PR. Shared collection previously skipped marked target exits. Billing now uses the measured client + target RX/TX sum, as requested, and shared quota uses the same accepted transaction deltas as period/history statistics. Allocation-specific sources and existing epoch/checkpoint acknowledgements isolate same-core users and prevent duplicate/replayed charges.

Port sync previously parsed saved drafts without checking the deployed instance revision. Save reconciliation could retire the running monitor; reserving a future port or removing a retired monitor could also stop the replacement instance. Discovery now reads confirmed ownership and exact deployed revisions, identifies pending changes separately, and rejects stale/foreign/undeployed candidates in a transaction. Deployment and sampling are coordinated per allocation. A policy refresh overlapping a queued deployment retains old rules and the persisted activation guard, then retries on authenticated reconnect. The regression reproduced the false stop before this correction and passes afterward. Final old counters/history and shared cumulative usage are retained; only settled, confirmed replacements retire old monitors. Actual revocation retains protective stops, and reservations follow the existing explicit owner release workflow.

The existing sync dialog shows old -> new, protocol, instance, config version, deployment status and blocked reasons. Rescan, selected and all selections use the same validated candidates. There are no new pages, audit tables, migrations or speculative historical data repair.

[Detailed root causes, configuration version handling, settlement strategy, real transfer measurements, screenshots and cleanup receipts](https://github.com/qimaoww/QControlHub/blob/5caa117251df3034a5b906c58a434a0305acf7e6/docs/shared-traffic-accounting/README.md).

title: fix: isolate multi-user core logs and add authorized instance filters
recorded_scope:
## Summary

Fix multi-user core log collection and enforce log-specific resource authorization. Started on main `c8115c3dd53c34491d3ccc7617378b1411f6abc8`, then merged latest main `05f04319` after its concurrent task migration; implementation and screenshots correspond to `d744ec66507cca722d109aae1f0afdc922406262`.

### Actual causes and collection repair

- Template unit parsing already existed, but the startup source snapshot contained only base services. Shared services deployed later never joined journal subscriptions. OpenRC's fixed file source list also omitted shared services.
- Node/engine-only identity could not separate recipients; node-administration authorization denied recipients and allowed administrators to see private user-owned nodes.
- Actual service tests additionally reproduced equal-size fast truncate/refill loss on OpenRC and empty/retired journal cursor recovery failures after rotation/vacuum.
- Discover protected shared configurations dynamically, subscribe before deployment, retain managed path/service/file permission checks, and isolate cursors, health and queue pressure per instance. Cover all four supported cores on systemd and OpenRC.

### Permission and provenance rules

- Require `core-logs.read` plus a live resource grant; `agents.read` is unnecessary.
- Administrators see main/shared instances on nodes they own, plus legacy unassigned nodes. They cannot read private user-owned node logs or metadata, including via an accepted share.
- Ordinary users see their own node's main instance and their own authorized shared instances. Other recipients' identities, services and logs remain inaccessible.
- Agent-authenticated node identity, canonical service/instance identity and the deployment/share ledger determine ownership; installer identity and uploaded owner fields do not.
- Schema 75 stores instance, service, instance owner and node owner at ingestion, with an instance covering index and independent source states. Ownership transfer does not transfer historical logs.
- Pre-upgrade history without verifiable provenance is retained as `unverified` and hidden. Legacy Agent uploads remain node-scoped and explicitly unattributed, never assigned to a shared user or main-instance filter. Shared nodes require an Agent upgrade (`core-log-instances-v1`).
- Apply the same scope to aggregate/node/user/instance queries, engine/level/search, history, source options, status, polling and existing GET data retrieval. There is no separate core-log export route in the current project. Recheck authorization before ETag comparison and before reusing UI caches.

### Existing log page

Add node and user/instance controls using existing native selects, typography and toolbar styles. Preserve valid selections and clear invalid ones, abort stale requests, clear revoked/account caches, and distinguish empty, waiting, failed, unsupported and denied states. Mobile controls wrap with existing touch navigation.

title: fix(ip-quality): repair legacy task constraints and report creation failures
recorded_scope:
## Summary

Repair IP quality HTTP 500 failures caused by a historical `tasks_check` that survives beside `tasks_engine_check`. Branch starts from latest main `c8115c3d`.

### Root cause and schema v74

- The old inline engine CHECK references both `action` and `engine`, so PostgreSQL names it **`tasks_check`**. Dropping/replacing `tasks_engine_check` never removed that original rule.
- The old rule allows an empty engine only for `upgrade-agent`; the newer named rule allows `upgrade-agent`, `enable-bbr`, `disable-bbr`, `configure-tcp`, and `ip-quality`. Both checks apply, so an otherwise valid new task fails with SQLSTATE **23514** before commit/Agent dispatch.
- `62da8cf3` (schema v69) and `c8115c3d` (v73) use the same empty-engine IP quality request and engine definition. This is an installation-history-dependent defect, not a newly changed detection parameter. The exact reporter installation lineage was unavailable; the isolated PostgreSQL reproduction confirms the structural cause.
- Fresh v73 bootstrap was verified separately: it creates **both** names too, but both engine rules are modern, so fresh success does not validate upgrade safety.

| State | Task CHECK set |
| --- | --- |
| Affected upgraded v69/v73 | restrictive `tasks_check` + modern `tasks_engine_check` + action/status/automatic-install checks |
| Fresh v73 | permissive `tasks_check` + modern `tasks_engine_check` + action/status/automatic-install checks |
| Fresh or upgraded v74 | exactly `tasks_action_check`, `tasks_engine_check`, `tasks_status_check`, `tasks_install_if_missing_check` |

Bump schema **73 -> 74**, so already-applied v73 databases execute the repair. Under the existing advisory lock and migration transaction, remove only the confirmed superseded `tasks_check`, then apply the canonical schema. Explicit names in `CREATE TABLE` prevent the unnamed duplicate from returning. Named action, engine, status, config revision/automatic-install, PK/FK and other integrity rules remain. Unrelated custom checks are preserved. Manual repairs and partial constraint sets are supported with `IF EXISTS`. Failures retain step context, roll back DDL/data/ledger, and retry on restart.

### API and page feedback

- Validated task insertion rejected by a known action/engine constraint returns HTTP **500**, stable `task_schema_incompatible`, `stage=task_creation`, and `request_id` / `X-Request-ID`. The existing `error` remains compatible with older clients and explains that Agent execution has not started and control-plane migrations need checking.
- Logs contain SQLSTATE, constraint, table/schema, action, Agent ID and correlation ID. Preserve operation wrappers needed by login diagnostics while excluding PostgreSQL messages/Detail, failing rows and SQL arguments. Other 23514 violations keep their own semantics.
- Reuse existing buttons, alerts, status labels and report components. Show creation, queue, execution, actual elapsed time and terminal states, with a minutes/network/probe-source hint and no fabricated percentage. The current Agent transport has no live phase updates; its stage diagnostics arrive with the final result, so running views show actual status/timing.
- Restore buttons after creation failure, retain an independent inline error and the last successful report, block duplicate in-flight requests, and adopt the confirmed POST task immediately even if the following history read fails. Manual/scheduled checks share creation and lifecycle logic.

Details, constraint definitions, deployment instructions and all four matched screenshot pairs: [upgrade investigation and evidence](https://github.com/qimaoww/QControlHub/blob/23a2c351/docs/ip-quality-upgrade-v74.md).

Same data, theme and running state in both versions; fixed comparison clock and an 83-second elapsed fixture, not a detection-time promise. Desktop: 1440x1000. Mobile: 375x900 with touch emulation.

title: fix(tls): align managed deployment with upstream and persist Caddy state
recorded_scope:
## Summary

Fix managed sing-box TLS deployment and audit the workflow against [233boy/sing-box at 2d78583b5aecccb0da0148a816bc1495a284509f](https://github.com/233boy/sing-box/tree/2d78583b5aecccb0da0148a816bc1495a284509f), especially `src/core.sh`, `src/caddy.sh`, `src/systemd.sh`, installation, downloads, generated configuration and lifecycle operations. Branch starts from current main `1786489a3aad922903ef32fbefbb7e10a5ae9dd0`.

### Failure diagnosis

- The Let's Encrypt directory request timeout is the direct certificate acquisition failure. The screenshot does not identify which network component caused it.
- `unable to get instance ID` / `mkdir /nonexistent: read-only file system` is a separate Caddy application data warning. Custom certificate storage does not configure the default application data directory. Fix both explicitly while retaining the existing certificate storage location.
- Missing email means the configured ZeroSSL automatic EAB fallback is unavailable. It does not cause the primary directory timeout.
- `tls: internal error` is the downstream handshake symptom when no usable certificate is ready. Core validation and an active process are insufficient deployment success criteria.

### Changes

- Give non-root Caddy explicit HOME, XDG data/config directories and a working directory inside `/var/lib/qcontrolhub-tls`. Keep restrictive systemd permissions, OpenRC capabilities and the existing `/var/lib/qcontrolhub-tls/caddy` certificate/account/lock storage.
- Recognize exact historical project service templates, preserve a backup, reload init configuration and restart only previously running services. Repair at Agent startup and before deployment. Preserve certificates and renewal state; reject modified units/drop-ins with actionable guidance. Use a pending marker for interrupted migration.
- Preflight DNS A/AAAA, public records, local listener conflicts, actual service-user write access, dependency capabilities and outbound ACME directory DNS/TCP/TLS. Report NAT/CDN and the limits of local/outbound checks. Reuse valid trusted cached certificates during CA outages.
- Validate the core before issuance. Prepare new certificates while retaining committed routes and old HTTPS listeners; HTTP-01 can complete while an outgoing proxy still owns the HTTPS port. Apply business configuration only after certificates are available.
- Bound primary and backup readiness to 65 seconds each. Reload affected domains to backup-only policy if primary work consumes its window, then restore the normal renewal chain after success. Keep account-default/preset email precedence and immutable encrypted snapshots. Use a six-minute managed operation and twelve-minute lease with independent rollback time.
- Complete Caddy HTTP/H2 generation, h2c backend, capability negotiation, deployment and client export. Add explicit externally managed TLS mode. Verify actual WS/HTTPUpgrade/H2 route handshakes after trusted TLS.
- Snapshot proxy content and init runtime/enablement state. Restore them on failure, retain other users' routes and certificates, and report original failure and recovery separately. Commit the manifest only after readiness succeeds.
- Reuse existing task/form components and themes. Show failure phase, classified cause, repair action and rollback result before expandable logs; wrap long content and contain log scrolling.

### Upstream behavior -> project status -> difference -> resolution

| Random preset credentials/path/backend; public TLS 443 | Native catalog, editable defaults and versioned metadata | H2 was native only | Complete managed H2; retain native mode for existing configurations. |

title: fix(core): enable authorized first installation and private preparation
recorded_scope:
## Summary

Fix first core installation across node settings and add-inbound validation/deployment without expanding the account permission model. Originally reproduced against main at 1786489a; synchronized with main at 0f2bc1a8 (managed TLS/Caddy deployment fixes) before merging.

### Reproduction and root cause

Reproduced against PostgreSQL with actual ordinary-user password logins, session cookies and CSRF middleware, rather than compatibility operator tokens:

- Owner with tasks.execute: manual installation already returned 201 on main. Preserve this contract; the fix adds consistent eligibility, progress, readable errors, retry and runtime refresh.
- Accepted share recipient manually installing a missing core: returned 403 on main. Now returns 201 for controlled preparation of the stable core, preserves the share identity and reuses any installed version. Uninstall, stop, start, restart and version switching remain forbidden to recipients.
- Accepted share recipient adding an inbound with install_if_missing=true: returned 403 on main. The frontend canAutoInstall, store requireAgentAdministration and Agent task/executor guards all treated installation preparation as host administration.
- Session permissions match durable user grants. Permission updates invalidate old sessions; matrix tests log in again. agents.manage alone does not confer node ownership or host administration.

### Changes and permission conditions

- Frontend: reuse the existing forms, buttons, confirmation and task monitor. Apply one operation-specific eligibility check during render, refresh and submit; distinguish execution permission, host scope, unsupported/disabled capabilities, legacy Agent features, offline state and pending work. Track manual installation and refresh versions/actions after completion; retain full failure text and allow retry. Fix narrow-screen form clipping using existing layout/style tokens.
- Manual host installation requires tasks.execute plus existing owner/admin management scope. Reading task status separately requires tasks.read; execute-only users can submit and receive an explicit status-visibility explanation.
- Shared manual installation requires tasks.execute, an accepted and enabled share granting the engine, an available allowance and the negotiated shared preparation features. The existing form offers only the stable channel; preparation cannot switch an installed version or start/stop the host service. Destructive and lifecycle actions remain owner-only.

## Summary

- Reuse Vision/Reality and the existing XHTTP/Reality preset. Add native Xray TLS/CDN, both mixed upload/download directions, and an optional five-in-one deployment.
- The two simplified standalone deployments use Xray directly, with no Nginx/Caddy dependency. Add Reality targets/SNI allowlists, separate address/port/SNI/Host/ALPN, IPv6 upload/IPv4 download and reversal, and independent TLS/CDN endpoints.
- Mixed and five-in-one deployments use one public Raw/Reality listener, an owned loopback TLS target in managed Nginx, and one loopback XHTTP backend. The fallback uses xver=0 and both paths reach the same backend. Mixed deployments omit the Vision user. Use isolated loopback TCP instead of world-writable Unix sockets.
- Preserve complete downloadSettings, xmux, server/client extras, certificate references, and group identity through encrypted versioned metadata and atomic paired configuration files. Reconcile group edits, renames, routing policies, exports and deletion together.
- Enforce listener isolation, allocated/shared ports, agent capabilities, source-bound local targets, non-root certificate access, syntax checks, service probes and rollback. Use authenticated user statistics to avoid charging the public relay and internal XHTTP traffic twice.
- Keep existing UI components and theme tokens; group basic fields and collapsible advanced settings. Provide five separate full Xray JSON exports with reveal/copy/download and explicit format compatibility reasons.

Usage, dependency table, source/version comparisons, actual screenshots, certificate/CDN trust requirements and rollback instructions: [XHTTP guide](docs/xray-xhttp-presets.md).

### Quick use and compatibility

1. Update Agent, use Xray 26.3.27, then choose an independent or combined XHTTP preset in the node's Xray server builder.
2. Reality alone needs a valid public target. Native TLS needs a readable certificate/key and valid SNI. CDN endpoints additionally require DNS, strict HTTPS origin trust and streaming/cache rules.
3. Mixed/five-in-one additionally require managed Nginx, two distinct internal ports, different Reality/TLS names and a certificate covering all configured names.
4. Save/deploy, then open client parameter details to copy/download each full JSON.
5. For shared nodes, the owner installs Xray and grants the engine and required ports, then the recipient accepts the invitation and uses their own workspace. Native presets need one public listener; mixed/five-in-one need the public listener plus both internal ports. Only the public port needs external ingress. Certificate references must be prepared with the managed service group permissions. Shared deployments use private core services and isolated managed proxy associations.

Basic XHTTP requires Xray >=24.12.15; use tested 26.3.27 for newer xmux fields. Normal VLESS XHTTP has empty flow; VLESS Encryption retains its separate rules. Basic Mihomo 1.19.32 exports are connection tested; its HTTP/1.1 + stream-one combination is disabled after a failed live test. Complex extras are Xray JSON only: Mihomo's download-settings/reuse-settings are not mapped by this exporter. Official sing-box 1.14.3 has no XHTTP transport.
